passage: I'm Zeenat, and I was doing homework at the table when it happened. Earlier Ammi had raised her voice at my little sister Dilnaz over the biscuit fight. At bedtime I saw Ammi sit on Dilnaz's bed. "I shouted today. I'm sorry. That wasn't kind of me." Dilnaz just nodded. Then they made a list with crayons: stomp like a soft cat, draw an angry picture, ask for a squeeze. Dilnaz practised the cat stomp, giggling. I can't say what was in her head, but she taped the list to the wall herself.

qa.q: What three ideas did Ammi and Dilnaz put on the list?
qa.a: Stomp like a soft cat, draw an angry picture, and ask for a squeeze.

qa.q: What might Dilnaz taping the list to the wall herself suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she feels some ownership of the plan and maybe pride, though Zeenat admits she can't be sure what was in her head.

qa.q: Why did Ammi's apology matter at this stage?
qa.a: By saying sorry for shouting, Ammi showed that grown-ups also make things right, which makes it easier for Dilnaz to repair after her own anger.

qa.q: How does Zeenat see the bedtime talk?
qa.a: She watches from the homework table as an outsider, noticing her sister's nod and giggle, and seems quietly glad the fight ended this way. 😊

grounding: An older sister watches a mother apologise for shouting and make a list of calm anger choices with a five-year-old.

passage:
Monday: Suraj flung his shoe after Papa said no to more jalebi. Naveen snapped, "Stop it!" louder than he meant.
Wednesday: At bedtime Naveen said, "I yelled on Monday. I'm sorry." Together they drew three pictures: soft stomping feet, a crayon scribble, two arms for a hug. Suraj stuck them on the fridge.
Saturday: Told no to a second ice cream, Suraj's face crumpled. He marched to the fridge, stomped softly, grabbed a crayon and scribbled hard. Then he walked over with his arms up. Naveen lifted him. "You used your plan," he whispered.

qa.q: What did Suraj do with the three pictures?
qa.a: Suraj stuck them on the fridge.

qa.q: What does Suraj walking over with his arms up on Saturday suggest he wanted?
qa.a: He wanted comfort after his anger and trusted that asking for a hug would be welcomed, just as the plan said.

qa.q: Which step on Wednesday set up Saturday's calmer moment?
qa.a: Naveen's apology plus drawing the three choices together gave Suraj concrete things to do with anger, and he remembered them days later.

qa.q: What might Naveen feel when Suraj uses the plan on Saturday?
qa.a: He likely feels proud and relieved, seeing that the talk after his own mistake helped his son handle a no better.

grounding: Across several days a father apologises for yelling and practises stomping, drawing and hugging with his son, who later uses the plan.

passage:
The power went off just as Sudha tucked Noor into bed, and the fan slowed to a stop. In the candle's small light, Sudha sat on the edge of the mattress.
"Noor, about the shouting today. I raised my voice too. I'm sorry."
Noor blinked. "Grown-ups say sorry?"
"Everyone can fix things. Next time you're angry, what could you do instead of kicking?"
Noor thought. "Stomp soft like a cat?"
"Yes. Or draw a cross face on paper. Or say 'hug please'."
In the heat, Noor stomped her feet softly on the sheet and giggled.

qa.q: What happened just as Sudha tucked Noor into bed?
qa.a: The power went off and the fan slowed to a stop.

qa.q: Why did Noor blink when Sudha apologised?
qa.a: She was surprised and curious that a grown-up would say sorry, which seemed new to her.

qa.q: What makes this talk a good turning point, and what could Sudha do tomorrow?
qa.a: It comes after the storm when both are calm, and tomorrow she could remind Noor of the soft stomp, drawing or asking for a hug.

qa.q: What is it like for Noor to hear her mother apologise?
qa.a: It probably feels reassuring, because it shows that making mistakes and fixing them is something everyone does.

grounding: Shows a mother talking through calmer ways to show anger, and apologising for her own raised voice, later that day.

passage:
On Sunday morning, in their Pune flat, Tarun spread paper and crayons across the floor. "Shalini, remember yesterday at the sweet shop?"
Shalini nodded, not looking up.
"You were angry. I was angry too, and I shouted. That wasn't okay. I'm sorry."
Shalini looked up then, surprised.
"Let's make a plan for angry times," Tarun said. They drew three pictures together: feet stomping softly, a crayon scribbling hard, two arms asking for a hug. Shalini stuck them on the fridge herself, the hug picture lowest, where she could reach it.

qa.q: Where did Shalini stick the pictures?
qa.a: On the fridge, with the hug picture lowest where she could reach it.

qa.q: What did Shalini's surprised look suggest when Tarun said sorry?
qa.a: She seemed surprised and perhaps relieved that her father admitted shouting too, so she did not carry all the blame.

qa.q: Which part of Tarun's plan works well for a young child, and why?
qa.a: Drawing the choices as pictures, because Shalini can see and point to them when she is too angry for words.

qa.q: How might Tarun feel after apologising to Shalini?
qa.a: He may feel lighter and hopeful, having modelled repair instead of pretending he did nothing wrong.

grounding: Shows a father apologising for shouting and drawing angry-time choices with his daughter, modelling repair.

passage:
"Pihu, can we talk about the stamping yesterday?" Sarita asked, snapping beans.
"I was very very cross."
"You were. And I yelled back. I'm sorry for my loud voice."
"Nani, Mummy said sorry!" Pihu announced.
Nirmala Nani laughed from her chair. "Good. Sorry is for everyone."
"So when you're cross next time," Sarita said, "what can you do?"
"Draw a monster?"
"Yes. What else?"
"Stomp softly... and ask for a hug."
"Shall we practise the soft stomp?"
Pihu stomped gently around the kitchen, and Nani joined in.

qa.q: What was Sarita doing while she talked to Pihu?
qa.a: Snapping beans.

qa.q: Why did Pihu announce "Mummy said sorry" to Nani?
qa.a: She seemed surprised and pleased that her mother apologised, and wanted to share that surprise.

qa.q: What small step could the family keep using after this talk?
qa.a: Practising the soft stomp and the other choices when calm, so Pihu can use them when she is cross.

qa.q: How does Nirmala Nani see this repair?
qa.a: Nani seems pleased and approving, saying sorry is for everyone and even joining the stomping.

grounding: Shows a mother apologising for yelling and practising softer ways to show anger with her daughter, joined by the grandmother.

passage: Note for Pooja's teacher, from her mother, Ganga. You asked how the angry mornings were going. Last night Pooja and I made an angry list together. She drew three pictures: feet stomping softly, a crayon scribbling hard on scrap paper, and two arms for "ask for a hug". I also told her, "This morning I raised my voice. I'm sorry. I'll try the list too." She looked surprised, then patted my cheek. Today, when her sock felt wrong, she stomped softly across the room, giggled and asked for a hug. The list is on our fridge. Could you try it at school?

qa.q: What three pictures did Pooja draw?
qa.a: Feet stomping softly, a crayon scribbling hard on scrap paper, and two arms for "ask for a hug".

qa.q: What did Pooja's pat on her mother's cheek suggest she felt?
qa.a: She seemed surprised and touched by the apology, and forgiving, glad her mother could say sorry too.

qa.q: Why is Ganga's apology part of the skill-building?
qa.a: By owning her raised voice, she shows Pooja that everyone can make things right, not only children.

qa.q: What might Pooja's teacher think on reading the note?
qa.a: The teacher may feel encouraged and ready to try the angry list at school so Pooja has the same tools there.

grounding: Shows a parent and child later planning what to do when angry, and the parent apologising for a raised voice, modelling repair.
